# Static geometry qualification

## Scope and entry state

This package qualifies the existing Default-heap implementation; it does not introduce GPU-local geometry as a new feature. Foundation PR #439 is integrated at `a761969668136f32ce99438e4b6a407094c9567e` (0.1.530). Current source, open PRs and ownership were rechecked before this branch: no open overlapping work. Required full `build-test` was still running; path ownership is not permission to merge or a waiver of CI. The historical ownership manifest is preserved unchanged. This PR changes only delegated tests/probes/qualification and the serial one-PATCH version preparation.

No redundant production transfer, allocation churn or retirement gap has been demonstrated by this qualification. No production implementation is changed, and no speedup is attributed to this PR. Existing capacity, ten-second fence bounds, failure policy, direct queue and global device/context lifetime stay intact.

## Static and dynamic caller audit

| Caller | Current behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `TerrainRenderer.cs:183` | Shared terrain indices use `CreateInitializedStaticBuffer`. |
| `TerrainRenderer.cs:255` | Terrain chunk vertices use the same native override; residency-driven chunk admission can upload later. |
| `SimpleInstanceRenderer.cs:149` and `:152` | Fallback cube vertices and indices already use initialized static buffers. |
| `AssetResidency/ResidentAssetStore.cs:701` and `:706` | Compiled object vertices and indices already use initialized static buffers. |
| `GpuParticleRenderer.cs:104` | Missed static caller: the six immutable UInt16 indices still use `CreateBuffer(Upload)` followed by `SetData`. Serial integration should replace only that 12-byte initialization with `CreateInitializedStaticBuffer(new(12, StaticGraphicsBufferUsage.Index), MemoryMarshal.AsBytes<ushort>(...))`, preserving disposal and index binding. No change here: Graphics renderer caller is outside this package. |

The native override in `ResourceScheduling/D3D12UploadArena.cs` allocates `HeapType.Default`, returns `GpuLocal`, consumes the CPU span before returning, batches copies, promotes Common to CopyDest and explicitly transitions to VertexAndConstantBuffer or IndexBuffer. Tests query native `GetHeapProperties`, then compare indexed native pixels. The interface default implementation remains a compatibility Upload path for other backends/doubles; it is not evidence of native heap selection.

Dynamic instance and shadow-instance buffers in `SimpleInstanceRenderer`, bone matrices in `SkinFrameCache`, particle instance frames, debug draw, UI text/skin batches and HUD/overlay vertices correctly remain Upload-backed because their contents change per admitted frame. `FrontendMenuBackground` also writes its per-frame vertices. Those callers and shared interfaces are read-only here.

## Ownership, ordering and failure contracts

Staging placements stay 512-byte aligned, with at most 32 destinations per batch. There are three 4 MiB normal slots and one growable large-transfer slot up to 128 MiB; maximum retained staging is 140 MiB. A slot is reusable only after its known submission fence completes. The arena selects the oldest fence under pressure rather than adding a queue or waiting for idle per resource.

Frame admission flushes pending copies before the draw command list; resource use also flushes an active upload batch. Destination lifetimes remain recorded until a successful queue Signal assigns their copy fence. Early wrapper disposal retains their native resource through copy completion, and subsequent draw fences extend last use. Execute/Signal uncertainty remains sticky and unresettable. Shutdown establishes actual queue idle before releasing retained ownership.

`StaticGeometryLifecycleTests` extends native coverage with actual heap properties, vertex/index state and first indexed draw, CPU input mutation, resident-frame transfer invariance, early/repeated wrapper disposal, 200 geometry lifecycle cycles, allocation/map/close/execute/signal failures, last-draw disposal and pending-copy shutdown. A real queue gate holds the three normal slots in flight; the fourth transfer must apply pressure and can reuse a slot only after an independent fence signal. Existing large-transfer/growth tests and pure boundary/unknown-fence tests remain unchanged.

## Measurement method and limits

Full-scene references use the unchanged integrated source, exact stamped Release binaries, the same AssetCompiler 1.13.0 payload and existing native host/collector. `DaylightTerrain` and `IndustrialBase`, seed 2026, NormalGameplay 420 m, Medium, 1920×1080 at native scale, VSync/debug/DRED off, 128 warmup frames, 512 samples and two repeated readbacks. Fixed and Traverse are separate cohorts, each run in Default/Upload/Upload/Default order in independent processes. Traverse is an additional residency diagnostic; it does not replace the foundation Fixed/Sweep scaling matrix or implement the benchmark package's planned 1k/10k/100k fixtures.

Every process-start value of `FORGELINE_STATIC_BUFFER_UPLOAD_FALLBACK` is recorded in a companion provenance JSON. Default is unset; fallback is exactly `1`. The exact previous environment value is restored after probe execution, and scene runners restore normal behavior afterward. Matched variants use the identical adapter, driver, payload, binary and source; companion identities supplement the unchanged collector. Captures require clean source and reject mismatched binary stamps. A first attempt started before the source rebuild had completed and was rejected by that guard; it has no qualified timing samples and is excluded from the matrix.

The extended existing upload probe is a separately labelled static geometry microdiagnostic, not a second reference host. It retains 128 pairs of 64 KiB vertex/16 KiB index buffers (10 MiB destination bytes), records native heap type and D3D12 Architecture1, and separates creation, first indexed submission and final fence drain. It then observes 64 warmup/256 fixed resident frames and 256 disposed streaming replacements. Immutable arena snapshots expose allocations, transfers/submissions, retained/peak staging bytes and pressure waits at every phase. CPU stopwatch intervals include driver/CPU work and waits; GPU-copy duration remains unavailable. This workload draws one indexed pair and does not represent total mesh rendering throughput.

Native correctness and performance settings are separate. Tests inspect debug-layer diagnostics when available and engine tracked live/pending resources; an unavailable optional debug layer is an explicit skip. The engine plateau is not a DXGI live-object report. No such report, PIX/ETW capture, thermal/background-load attribution, UMA performance cohort, live gameplay or sustained-FPS/human art acceptance is claimed. Raw GPU frame timing includes the existing renderer's passes and reports completed-fence counts, not copy-engine timing.

## Results and validation

The complete unchanged-source and instrumentation-source Release solution builds pass with zero warnings/errors. The current native ResourceScheduling selection passes 46 cases, fails none and explicitly skips two optional debug-layer cases (48 total). Ten new cases cover static geometry, with nine executed passes and one debug-layer skip. The pressure test observes real backpressure, three retained normal slots and reuse after the external queue gate is signalled. Native heap queries confirm Default, including indexed initial data consumption and stable first draw. The initially authored 0.5 UNORM pixel assertion expected byte 128; the adapter produces 127, so the new assertion checks the two adjacent representable UNORM bytes. Existing exact image equality assertions and production code are unchanged.

Hardware: Intel Core Ultra 9 285HX, 24 logical processors, NVIDIA RTX PRO 5000 Blackwell Generation Laptop GPU, 25,309,478,912 dedicated bytes, driver 32.0.15.9653, Windows 10.0.26300 x64, .NET 10.0.13 / SDK 10.0.402. D3D12 Architecture1 succeeds and reports UMA=false, cache-coherent UMA=false on this adapter. No integrated/UMA performance cohort is available. Catalog content signature is `135b44877d4882ac539073738a43af7b4794ff35819cc2c1f55c353771743020`; the existing whole-directory runtime fingerprint is `55827DADD0271F6F74F0FB66E2B2774C924C38FC106B6EA351C43BF9A694EBBA`. These are different identity algorithms.

All eight scene processes qualify structurally: 16 cases, 8,192 raw CPU frames, explicit completed GPU-fence counts, two matching native readbacks per case, no submission/material/fallback-mesh failures. All Traverse images and both Default Fixed processes are byte-identical for matching cases. The first Upload Fixed process differs from the other three processes in each scene by one channel value at one pixel (1 / 2,073,600 pixels, channel delta 1). The second Upload Fixed process matches Default exactly. Eight strict pixel-comparison reports retain the differences; zero-tolerance acceptance is not granted or relaxed, and no cause is assigned from heap selection alone. Original PNGs remain in the local capture artifacts with hashes bound in each retained manifest; the embedded archive retains JSON samples/reports, not PNG binaries. Human visual review remains pending.

## Static upload microdiagnostic

Source `d2559233f32f757ee01cbd80c500242c43b4453e` is clean and contains the final test/probe implementation; all production rendering source blobs equal integrated master. Every final probe binary carries that source identity and is hash recorded. Final documentation and PATCH preparation do not relabel measured binaries. Earlier pre-control probes (retained separately) recorded an empty string for the Default override and restored an absent variable as an empty string. The final controller uses the environment provider to remove an absent override and verifies normal absence after successful and intentionally failing child runs; the production Default selector itself is unchanged.

Each process holds exactly 10 MiB of destination buffers; fallback destination memory is Upload, not Default. Fixed resident frames add **zero** staging transfers, submissions, allocations or retained bytes in both modes. All four resident images have identical byte hashes. The streaming phase adds a new 10 MiB of destinations, disposes them and drains retirement; it is not hidden in the fixed resident interval.

Default has explicit one-time staging/copy cost; Upload has no arena copies. CPU creation/drain samples do not establish GPU-copy duration or a universal initialization advantage. All probes return to their pipeline-only tracked resource plateau, with no pending retirement or submission faults. Normal measured pressure waits can be zero on this adapter; deterministic native queue-gate coverage separately tests the pressure path. The existing deferred-texture probe also passes after the CLI extension and retains its legacy schema and semantics.

## Reproduction and handoff

Build the current source before hardware qualification. Use the existing reference script with `-Capture -Scenes DaylightTerrain,IndustrialBase -Profiles Medium -Zooms NormalGameplay -Displays 1920x1080 -Warmups 128 -Samples 512 -RepeatCaptures 2`, first `-CameraPath Fixed`, separately `Traverse`, with the same explicit runtime payload and frozen client. Start independent processes in Default/Upload/Upload/Default order, recording the environment before process creation and restoring it in `finally`.

For the microdiagnostic, run `Measure-Uploads.ps1 -ClientDirectory <frozen-client> -OutputRoot <fresh-artifacts-path> -SourceSha <full-built-commit> -Workload StaticGeometry`, adding `-StaticBufferUploadFallback` only for the middle pair. `-Workload Texture` remains the default legacy workload. The script rejects inherited diagnostic overrides and restores its own temporary fallback override even after failure.

Run the canonical SDK-selected test runner: `dotnet test --project tests/ForgeLine.Graphics.Tests/ForgeLine.Graphics.Tests.csproj -c Release --no-build -- --filter-class '*ResourceScheduling*'`. Validate this lane with the existing ownership validator and exact `StaticGeometryQualification` package. Only serial finalization edits `Directory.Build.props`, once for this PR. Required complete CI remains a merge prerequisite; no merge, tag, protection or caller changes are included.

Serial integration handoff: migrate the immutable 12-byte particle index buffer at `src/ForgeLine.Graphics/GpuParticleRenderer.cs:104–105` through the existing initialized-static Index contract. No new interface or capacity change is required. Debug-layer/native live-object evidence and a UMA machine remain unavailable qualification items rather than successful checks.

Final source checks: 46 project references with no cycles; nine ownership/factory contract tests pass; the six delegated paths validate against StaticGeometryQualification. The serial version preparation is exactly 0.1.530 → 0.1.531. Native correctness was rebuilt and rerun from clean source 14d312d79844ed1f08346eb83bb623890c460146 (46 pass, two explicit skips); the unchanged interface compatibility selection additionally passes both cases. The pressure test's independent fence helper observes actual backpressure before signalling, with no sleep-based assumption about owner scheduling.

Concurrent-work recheck: [PR #440](https://github.com/DaveBeusing/Forgeline/pull/440) contains only its instancing tests, CPU benchmark and qualification document plus Directory.Build.props. No delegated geometry path overlaps. Central version preparation remains serialized at integration; the PR merged second must rebase and allocate its one PATCH against the then-current master. Master is still a761969668136f32ce99438e4b6a407094c9567e; its full build-test is running at this recheck, with navigation and conveyor successful. No historical failure or partial result is represented as successful complete CI.
